name: Spot reduction exercises

lead: Spot reduction is the idea that exercising one area, like the abs or the face, burns fat in that area for a slimmer belly, cheeks or jawline. It is promoted in fitness media and looksmaxxing spaces as ab routines and face or jaw exercises.

Proponents think working a muscle draws on nearby fat. Researchers cited by reference works say fat is mobilised from the whole body according to overall energy balance, genetics and hormones; a 2022 meta-analysis of 13 studies found no significant localized fat reduction, and a small 2023 trial suggested a possible exception. Building muscle in an area can change how it looks.

paras: Users do crunch and ab circuits, or facial and jaw exercises, usually alongside a diet aimed at overall fat loss.
Little direct harm is documented. The cited concern is misleading marketing, including ab-belt claims the FTC has challenged and EMS devices not FDA-cleared for fat loss.

angle.text: Users train one area, such as the abs or jaw, hoping to burn fat there for a slimmer belly, cheeks or jawline. Studies cited by reference works find fat is lost across the body, though building muscle in an area can change its look.

lead: Spot reduction is the belief that exercising a particular body area, such as crunches for the abdomen or facial exercises for the cheeks, preferentially burns fat stored over that area.[1][2] It is widely marketed in fitness media, and in looksmaxxing communities it appears as ab routines and face or jaw exercises aimed at a leaner look.

Wikipedia describes the claim as pseudoscientific and states that the consensus among physiologists and fitness professionals is that fat loss occurs across the body with diet and exercise.[1] Grokipedia reports that a 2022 meta-analysis of 13 studies found no significant localized fat reduction, while noting a small 2023 trial that suggested a possible exception.[2]
infobox: Claim about exercise and fat distribution
Ab exercises, thigh exercises, facial exercises
Spot toning (building muscle in an area)
Fat loss is systemic, not local[1][2]

paras: Spot reduction contrasts with spot toning, which means building muscle in an area to change its firmness and definition rather than to remove overlying fat.[2] Where fat is stored and lost first is described as strongly influenced by genetics, sex and hormones; the lower abdomen, lower back and flanks are commonly cited as slow to lose fat.[1][2]

Grokipedia traces area-specific reducing exercises to early physical culture figures such as Eugen Sandow and to Bernarr Macfadden's magazines in the 1920s and 1930s, followed by post-war vibrating belts and reducing garments, then 1980s and 1990s workout videos, the ThighMaster and infomercial ab devices.[2] Social media, HIIT content and electrical muscle stimulation devices are cited as modern carriers of the idea.[2]

Grokipedia states that facial fat does not respond to targeted exercise and that facial exercises build muscle without reducing fat; it adds that lower water retention can make the face look slimmer in the short term.[2] Proponents of face and jaw exercises, by contrast, say that toning facial muscles changes contour.

Studies described by Wikipedia and Grokipedia include a comparison of tennis players' arms, in which the dominant forearm was larger from muscle but skinfold measurements showed no difference in fat between arms.[1][2] In a 2011 randomized trial in the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 24 sedentary adults did abdominal exercises five days a week for six weeks; abdominal subcutaneous fat did not decrease, though core endurance improved.[1]

Grokipedia lists further work: a 1984 sit-up study in 20 adults over 27 days with no significant abdominal fat loss, a 2007 upper-body training study in 104 people in which MRI showed generalized rather than local fat loss, and a 2022 meta-analysis of 13 studies (1,158 participants) finding no significant localized fat reduction.[2] It also describes a 2023 trial in 16 overweight men in which adding abdominal endurance work to running gave greater trunk fat loss, presenting it as a small, male-only study not yet replicated.[2] These secondary summaries were not checked against the original papers.
Grokipedia states that the US FDA has not cleared electrical muscle stimulation devices for spot fat loss and that the Federal Trade Commission has challenged misleading ab-belt claims.[2]

lore.intro: Community discussion of ab and face exercises was not reviewed for this entry; the claims below are those described in encyclopedic sources about the wider belief.

claims.claim: Doing ab exercises burns belly fat.
Facial exercises slim the face or jaw.
Adding core work to cardio may speed trunk fat loss.

timeline.event: Magazines and figure-correction books promote area-specific reducing exercises.[2]
Sit-up study in sedentary adults reports no significant abdominal fat loss.[2]
Randomized trial of six weeks of abdominal exercise finds no reduction in abdominal subcutaneous fat.[1]
Meta-analysis of 13 studies reports no significant localized fat reduction.[2]
Small trial in overweight men suggests added trunk fat loss with abdominal work.[2]
